A township of villages, and an address that confuses outsiders

The Woodlands had 114,436 residents in the 2020 census, which is bigger than many Texas cities, yet it is not a city. It is run by The Woodlands Township, a special purpose district created after the Texas Legislature passed enabling legislation in 2007, with a seven-member board elected by voters in both Montgomery and Harris counties. Residents voted on becoming a city in November 2021, and about two thirds said no.

Inside the township, people identify by village. The Township lists village associations including Alden Bridge, Cochran's Crossing, College Park, Creekside Park, Grogan's Mill, Indian Springs, Panther Creek and Sterling Ridge, and its website offers an address lookup to find which village an address belongs to. Creekside Park is the only village that reaches into Harris County.

For someone in Ohio or California, none of that is obvious. A web design The Woodlands TX newcomers can follow says it plainly: which villages you serve, what the mailing address really is, and how far you will drive.

Why so many of your customers are still packing boxes

Big employers keep pulling households into the area. ExxonMobil announced in 2022 that it would move its corporate headquarters from Irving to its large campus in Spring. Hewlett Packard Enterprise moved its global headquarters to a campus in the CityPlace development in Spring in 2022, and the company said then that it had about 2,200 employees in the Houston area.

Households relocating for jobs like these research before they arrive. That favors the business whose site answers questions without a phone call: services in plain words, prices or a price range where you can give one, photos of the real place, and an easy way to book.

What a newcomer-ready site in The Woodlands should show

  • Your village or the villages you cover, written out, not just "Houston area".
  • Whether you are near Town Center, where the Waterway connects Market Street, Waterway Square, Hughes Landing and The Woodlands Mall, or out in the neighborhoods.
  • Hours, parking and whether walk-ins are welcome, for people who have never been inside.
  • A short "new to the area?" note if you take new patients, students or members.
  • A contact form that emails you, and a phone number that rings.

A salon, a gym, a tutoring center or a dental office gets judged from a phone screen by people choosing among several options at once. Clear photos and a page that says who you serve do more than a clever slogan. Google's own guidance says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence, and naming the villages you truly serve helps with the first two.

Local help for Woodlands owners

The Woodlands Area Chamber of Commerce began in 1978 as the South Montgomery County Woodlands Chamber, took its current name in 2012, and says it represents more than 1,300 area employers. For one-on-one advice, the Lone Star College Small Business Development Center offers free business consulting and low-cost workshops across the college's service area, which includes The Woodlands.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in The Woodlands. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

That also means no showroom visit to sit through. You get a demo link, Maurice answers questions, and you approve every page before it goes live.

Common questions

Who does web design in The Woodlands, TX for small businesses?

Plenty of firms around Houston do. Dominion Web Design Pro is one person, Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes and builds every site by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. He has no office in The Woodlands, so everything happens by link, phone and email. You see a free demo of your site before you decide anything.

Is The Woodlands a city? What should my website call it?

Not legally. The Woodlands is governed by The Woodlands Township, a special purpose district, and voters turned down incorporation in November 2021. On your site, call it The Woodlands, name the village you are in or serve, and use your real mailing city and ZIP code in the address. Customers and Google both read those details.

How much does a website cost for a business in The Woodlands?

Our prices are printed and paid once: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for a page for each town and service the keyword research says is worth having. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent, which is $297 a month after its free trial.

Can my site have separate pages for Creekside Park, Spring and Conroe?

Yes, if you really serve those places. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written for that place, so a page about Creekside Park can talk about Creekside Park and not just repeat your home page with a new name on it.
